title: Static routes between two routers
summary: Make two LANs reach each other through a point-to-point link by writing static routes on both routers.
objectives: Read which networks a router already knows
Write a static route with the right next hop
Remember that traffic needs a route in both directions

tasks.title: Route from R1 to the R2 LAN
tasks.description: R1 only knows its own networks. Tell it that 203.0.113.0/24 is reached through R2 at 192.0.2.2.
hints: A static route needs a destination network, its mask and the address of the next router.
The next hop must be an address on a network R1 is directly connected to.
Example on R1: system-view, then ip route-static 203.0.113.0 24 192.0.2.2

tasks.title: Route from R2 to the R1 LAN
tasks.description: A ping needs a reply. Give R2 a route to 198.51.100.0/24 through R1 at 192.0.2.1.
hints: The request can arrive and still fail: the reply has to find its way back.
Example on R2: ip route-static 198.51.100.0 24 192.0.2.1 (a mask such as 255.255.255.0 works too)

tasks.title: Verify reachability
tasks.description: Both PCs must now reach each other and the far end of the link.
hints: If a check fails, compare the next hop on each router with the address of the other router on the link.

criteria.label: PC1 reaches the far end of the link (192.0.2.2)
